# Onboarding path admission

Student is the authoritative owner of the S9 no-active-path admission decision.
The feature is disabled by default with `STUDENT_ONBOARDING_PATH_ADMISSION_ENABLED=false`.
Before migration 025, flag-off startup does not query either admission table. After
the migration exists, ordinary path writers also honour a live reservation while
the API remains flag-off, so rollback is flag-off plus drain rather than schema
removal.

All routes below require the dedicated `LEARNING_PLANNER_INTERNAL_TOKEN`, exactly
one canonical UUID `Idempotency-Key`, `Content-Type: application/json`, strict
unknown-field/trailing-body rejection, and canonical UUID route IDs. A malformed
`studentID` is `400 invalid_student_id`; a malformed `admissionID`, header, or body
is `422 invalid_request`. The reserve,
renew, and abort bodies are capped at 64 KiB; materialization is capped at 1 MiB.
No browser route is registered. The disabled service returns `503`
`onboarding_path_admission_disabled` before accessing an admission table.

## Contract

`POST /internal/students/{studentID}/onboarding-path-admissions` accepts
`student-onboarding-path-admission-request.v1` with canonical `handoff_id` and
`execution_id`, the exact authoritative readiness `expected_state_ref`, and the
versioned `{code,version,graph_version}` goal. It returns
`student-onboarding-path-admission.v1`, status `RESERVED`, a fence, and a lease
expiry. In the same Student transaction, the command holds the shared per-student
admission fence, locks the exact draft/profile state-reference row, and verifies there is no
`student_learning_path` with `status='ACTIVE'`.

`POST .../{admissionID}/renewal` accepts
`student-onboarding-path-admission-renewal.v1` with the execution ID and current
fence. Its own idempotency receipt returns the same renewed fence/expiry after a
lost ACK. A valid execution may renew an expired reservation only after the same
state/no-active-path checks under that lock; it receives a new fence. Old fences
cannot materialize or abort.

`PUT .../{admissionID}/materialization` accepts
`student-onboarding-path-admission-materialization.v1`:

```json
{"schema":"student-onboarding-path-admission-materialization.v1","execution_id":"uuid","fence":1,"course":{"course_id":"uuid","course_fingerprint":"frozen","planner_policy_version":"v1","reason_code":"initial","reason_summary":"bounded"},"lessons":[{"lesson_id":"uuid","targets":[{"type":"concept","key":"go.http","version":"v1"}]}]}
```

It atomically creates the course assignment, exactly one primary `ACTIVE` path,
one `READY` first item, remaining `PLANNED` items, the initial path revision and
selected context. The response schema is deliberately different:
`student-onboarding-path-materialization.v1`; it includes the stable
`first_lesson_id`, assignment/path IDs, and path/journey revisions.

`POST .../{admissionID}/abort` accepts
`student-onboarding-path-admission-abort.v1` with execution ID, fence, and one
of `NO_GAP`, `STATE_CHANGED`, `ACTIVE_PATH_EXISTS`, or `CANCELLED`. It reaches a
durable `ABORTED` no-gap terminal state and creates neither assignment nor path.

Exact replays return their stored response only with the same idempotency key,
operation, student, and request hash. Reusing a handoff or terminal operation with
a new key, or reusing any key with changed content, conflicts. State drift,
an existing active path, a stale fence/lease, and missing admissions map to
`state_changed`, `active_path_exists`, `reservation_expired`, and
`admission_not_found`; malformed commands map to `invalid_request`.

Migration `025_student_onboarding_path_admission.sql` keeps request/operation
evidence write-once, only allows reservation renewal or terminal transitions, and
prevents delete/truncate. The empty-only rollback proof is deliberately kept as
[`onboarding-path-admission-rollback.sql`](onboarding-path-admission-rollback.sql)
outside the production migration glob. Once evidence exists, operational rollback
is feature flag-off and lease drain; it never deletes evidence.
